Egy ország vízháztartását az dönti el, m: What decides a country's water household is how long the water stays. River water moves on within a week: what enters at Devín today passes Mohács next week. Water that reaches the soil stays for weeks. What seeps deeper stays for decades. The same cubic metre is worth something different in each of the three places — which is why the Danube can run high while the fields go dry. The Middle Danube Basin is unusually good ground for this, because it is an almost closed hydrological box: water enters at Devín, leaves at the Iron Gate, and the catchments of the Tisza, the Drava and the Sava lie entirely inside. Its balance can therefore be written down. Which of its terms we can actually measure is a separate question — and this page reports on that too.
